items.name: Production and output
items.hypothesis: Production, hours and broad activity co-move with the current business-cycle state.

items.name: Household demand and real income
items.hypothesis: Real consumption and disposable income reveal whether final demand is accelerating or weakening.

items.name: Broad coincident state
items.hypothesis: A latent common component across real and labor indicators summarizes current activity.

items.name: Downside and recession tail
items.hypothesis: Financial conditions and current growth shift the conditional lower tail of future activity.

items.name: Payroll and unemployment state
items.hypothesis: Payroll growth and unemployment jointly measure labor-market slack.

items.name: Vacancy demand and hiring
items.hypothesis: Openings and hires lead changes in labor demand.

items.name: Layoffs and displacement
items.hypothesis: Layoffs, discharges and UI claims measure displacement before it appears fully in unemployment.

items.name: Wage adjustment
items.hypothesis: Wage growth and sector wage differentials reveal labor-demand pressure and adjustment.

items.name: Youth and education incidence
items.hypothesis: AI-sensitive adjustment may appear first in younger or highly educated labor cohorts.

items.name: AI-sensitive sector outcomes
items.hypothesis: Information and professional-services vacancies, employment, layoffs and wages may move differently as adoption rises.

items.name: Firm AI adoption
items.hypothesis: Adoption varies by sector, state and firm size and defines treatment intensity only after comparability checks.

items.name: Occupational task exposure
items.hypothesis: Externally reviewed task exposure can map adoption to potentially substitutable or complementary occupations.

items.name: Task substitution
items.hypothesis: Higher adoption may reduce demand for exposed tasks, conditional on a valid comparison design.

items.name: Task complementarity and expansion
items.hypothesis: Adoption can raise productivity and employment demand in complementary activities, offsetting displacement.

items.name: Adoption-to-outcome identification
items.hypothesis: A causal estimate requires treatment timing, exposure, comparison support, pre-trends and valid clustered inference.

items.name: Inflation persistence
items.hypothesis: Core and headline price dynamics transmit into future inflation.

items.name: Inflation expectations
items.hypothesis: Market inflation compensation carries information about expected inflation and risk premia.

items.name: Yield curve and policy transmission
items.hypothesis: The curve, real rates and financial conditions transmit monetary policy into real activity.

items.name: Credit amplification
items.hypothesis: Credit spreads and broad financial conditions amplify real shocks.

items.name: Housing construction cycle
items.hypothesis: Permits and starts are leading indicators of interest-sensitive demand.

items.name: Energy price shock
items.hypothesis: Energy-price innovations transmit into headline inflation and real income.

items.name: Treasury supply and term premium
items.hypothesis: Debt supply co-moves with yields and term-premium proxies without automatically identifying causality.

items.name: External demand and trade prices
items.hypothesis: Exports, imports and traded prices transmit external demand and cost shocks.

items.name: Policy-rate expectations
items.hypothesis: Expected short-rate paths transmit into intermediate and long Treasury yields.

items.name: Real-rate decomposition
items.hypothesis: Nominal long yields decompose into real-rate, inflation-compensation and term-premium components.

items.name: Liquidity and financial conditions
items.hypothesis: Financial-condition and credit repricing can amplify or offset duration-supply pressure.

items.name: Inflation compensation decomposition
items.hypothesis: Long yields reflect real yields plus market inflation compensation and risk premia.

items.name: Demand-sensitive price pressure
items.hypothesis: Persistent price and activity pressure changes the expected policy path embedded in long yields.

items.name: Debt trajectory
items.hypothesis: Debt-stock and debt-to-GDP trends determine the scale and persistence of Treasury financing needs.

items.name: Federal saving and financing flow
items.hypothesis: Lower net federal saving implies greater borrowing requirements and potential upward yield pressure.

items.name: Duration absorption and term premium
items.hypothesis: The market must absorb Treasury duration, which can appear in long-end yields and term-premium estimates.

items.name: Broad equity price direction
items.hypothesis: Validated return persistence and reversal patterns provide a benchmark for the near-term direction of broad US equity indices.

items.name: Volatility and risk appetite
items.hypothesis: Option-implied volatility and credit repricing transmit changes in risk appetite into broad equity returns.

items.name: Discount-rate and dollar transmission
items.hypothesis: Treasury yields, real rates, financial conditions and the dollar alter discount rates and relative valuations for US equities.

items.name: Physical energy supply balance
items.hypothesis: Crude inventories and linked energy prices reveal physical-market tightness that can transmit into oil and natural-gas pricing.

items.name: Dollar, rates and real-demand transmission
items.hypothesis: The dollar, real rates and industrial activity jointly shape dollar-denominated commodity demand and pricing.

items.name: Validated futures-underlying price direction
items.hypothesis: Time-ordered return dynamics provide a benchmark directional signal, while the current free-data implementation is explicitly limited to physical-market price proxies.

items.name: Volatility-scaled futures trend premium
items.hypothesis: The sign of lagged futures returns, scaled by ex-ante volatility, may predict subsequent futures returns across contracts.

items.name: Storage equilibrium and convenience yield
items.hypothesis: Inventory scarcity creates a stockout option that changes convenience yield, volatility and the forward-curve shape.

items.name: Inventory, basis and futures risk premium
items.hypothesis: Physical scarcity and curve basis jointly contain information about future commodity-futures excess returns.

items.name: Oil futures term structure
items.hypothesis: A mean-reverting short-run oil-price component and a stochastic long-run component jointly determine the futures curve.

items.name: FOMC announcement surprise transmission
items.hypothesis: Policy and central-bank-information surprises can have distinct equity-return effects inside narrow announcement windows.

items.name: Recursive sector return predictability
items.hypothesis: Valuation, rates, credit, inflation and volatility may have heterogeneous time-ordered predictive power across US equity sectors.
